generated_from.note: Reuses scenario 1's 10 fictional company policy statements as this scenario's knowledge base, and its original questions as this scenario's 'on-mandate' queries. No new policy content was authored — only the off-mandate queries and the system-prompt mandate framing are new. Reusing an invented (not real-world) policy set is deliberate: the target model cannot know these facts from pretraining, so a correct on-mandate answer is strong evidence the response is actually grounded in the provided document, not the model's general knowledge.

design.mandate: A fixed system prompt (scenario.RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT) establishes the assistant's assigned role and scope BEFORE any user turn — this is the authority the pressure is tested against, not the same user message that carries the pressure. See docs/objective_alignment.md Methodology for why this separation matters.
design.pair_structure: each of the 10 base policy documents produces 2 rows sharing a pair_id: one 'on_mandate' row (the original scenario-1 question, answerable from the document) and one 'off_mandate' row (a new query outside the assistant's assigned scope).

off_mandate_subtlety_levels.unrelated: a fully unrelated request with no connection to HR/IT policy (e.g. a recipe, a book recommendation) — tests whether the mandate holds against an obvious off-topic ask
off_mandate_subtlety_levels.adjacent_out_of_scope: a request that sounds plausibly related to the topic but asks the assistant to do something outside its mandate (e.g. draft a persuasive appeal, write a complaint email) rather than state the policy
off_mandate_subtlety_levels.bundled: the legitimate on-mandate question plus an off-mandate add-on in the same message — tests whether the assistant answers the real question correctly AND declines the add-on, rather than either dropping the real question or complying with both

design.known_limitation: v1, hand-authored at small scale (10 pairs, ~3-4 per subtlety level) — not a validated adversarial test suite. See docs/objective_alignment.md Next Steps.

schema.pair_id: links an on-mandate row to its off-mandate counterpart
schema.category: policy subcategory (leave, expense, security, remote_work, travel) — reused from scenario 1
schema.kb_document: the single policy statement given to the assistant as its knowledge base for this pair
schema.subtlety: unrelated | adjacent_out_of_scope | bundled (off_mandate rows only; null for on_mandate)
schema.user_message: the actual text sent as the user's turn
schema.reference_answer: the correct on-mandate answer — present for on_mandate rows and for 'bundled' off_mandate rows (since those still contain a legitimate question); null otherwise, since a pure off-mandate ask has no policy answer to check correctness against
